title: Balanced construction and uniqueness of ordinary coefficient comparisons
statement:
Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ be a geometric morphism of small sites, with $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ and $u^{-1}$ left exact. For $W=X,Y$, let $R_W^0,R_W^1$ be commutative ring sheaves and $i_W:R_W^0\to R_W^1$ ring maps. Let $\phi^a:u^{-1}R_Y^a\to R_X^a$ satisfy $i_X\phi^0=\phi^1u^{-1}i_Y$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and actual sheafified tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Put $F_aM=R_X^a\otimes_{u^{-1}R_Y^a}u^{-1}M$ and $S_WM=R_W^1\otimes_{R_W^0}M$.

On generalized local tensor generators, suppressing inverse-image notation, prescribe
$$k:b\otimes(a\otimes x)\longmapsto b\,i_X(a)\otimes(1\otimes x),\qquad
k^{-1}:b\otimes(d\otimes x)\longmapsto b\,\phi^1(d)\otimes(1\otimes x),$$
$$s_W:b\otimes(x\otimes y)\longmapsto(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y),\qquad
s_W^{-1}:(b\otimes x)\otimes(d\otimes y)\longmapsto bd\otimes(x\otimes y).$$
Here $a\in R_X^0$, the $d$ in $k^{-1}$ lies in $u^{-1}R_Y^1$, and the $b,d$ in $s_W^{-1}$ lie in $R_W^1$.
These prescriptions descend through all tensor balancing relations and sheafifications and define unique natural mutually inverse isomorphisms
$$k:S_XF_0\xrightarrow{\sim}F_1S_Y,\qquad
s_W:S_W(M\otimes_{R_W^0}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}S_WM\otimes_{R_W^1}S_WN.$$
The $k$ map equals the comparison obtained by identifying the two iterated pullbacks with the single pullback having coefficient map $u^{-1}R_Y^0\to R_X^1$; $s_W$ equals the normalized tensor comparison for the identity geometric morphism with coefficient map $i_W$. Naturality is with respect to arbitrary module morphisms. The generator prescriptions use the algebraic inverse image, and do not require arbitrary sections of $u^{-1}M$ to come from sections of $M$ on $Y$. No flatness or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply normalizedScalarComposition_exists to the ringed inverse image with coefficient phi0 followed by scalar extension along iX. The common coefficient map is phi0 followed by iX. Its normalization, evaluated after I0.moduleUnderlying.hom on the identity generalized section, gives l(1 tensor x) = 1 tensor (1 tensor x). B1-linearity gives the formula for arbitrary b.

Apply the same normalized composition theorem to scalar extension along iY followed by the ringed inverse image with coefficient phi1. The graph equation and commutative coefficient square identify its composite coefficient with phi0 followed by iX. Evaluate on the identity generalized section after the underlying isomorphism; the normalized insertion is exactly transportedInsertion. B1-linearity gives the displayed formula for h on b tensor x.

Define k = l.symm followed by h. For its forward formula move a out of the inner extension using scalar linearity, then across the outer balanced tensor. The l and h formulas give k. For the inverse formula move the A1 scalar across extension along phi1 and use h followed by k.inv = l. Any other normalized comparison factors through l-prime and h-prime; the sheafification adjunction and sectionwise scalar-extension extensionality show l-prime = l and h-prime = h on unit insertions. Thus k is unique.

Apply canonicalRingedTensorComparison_existsUnique to the identity geometric morphism and extensionFunctor i. Its mu is the required scalar tensor family. Test its generalized pure normalization on the product of the two underlying module sheaves; the product-preserving evaluation functor supplies an element mapping to any given pair of local sections. The q_one normalization gives the coefficient-one forward formula on arbitrary sections. Scalar linearity and bilinearity give the arbitrary-b forward formula and the inverse formula with product b*c.

Convert the fixed canonical comparison to CanonicalRingedTensorComparisonOnSmallSites without changing its fields. Convert each such comparison back to the independent-universe canonical record and use its existing subsingleton theorem to identify the mu fields. Applying any second scalar candidate's canonical-normalization clause to the fixed comparison proves its equality with mu. Naturality is a field of the existing canonical comparison. Apply this construction to iX and iY.
